quarterly_data.signal: Positive high-level results from the DESTINY-Lung04 Phase III trial: AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo's Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan, 5.4mg/kg) showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (primary endpoint, assessed by blinded independent central review) versus the global standard of care (platinum-pemetrexed doublet chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab) as 1st-line treatment of unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with a HER2 exon 19 or 20 mutation. The trial (454 patients across Asia, Europe and North America, randomised 1:1) continues as planned to evaluate secondary endpoints including overall survival; safety was generally consistent with the known profile with no new safety concerns, and the data will be presented at a forthcoming medical meeting and shared with global regulatory authorities. Approximately 2-4% of NSCLC patients have tumours with a HER2 mutation. Enhertu is already approved in more than 80 countries for previously treated HER2-mutant NSCLC. The company calls Enhertu the first and only HER2-directed medicine to improve PFS over global standard of care in a Phase III trial in this setting (company claim).
